crossover.body: Chef Jozef Youssef's Kitchen Theory stages multi-sensory dinners where dishes are paired with soundscapes. At its Synaesthesia events the team found that glitchy music brought out bitter, sour and crunchy elements, while melodic music suited sweet and creamy ones. The work draws on research by Charles Spence's group at Oxford, which found that high piano tones raise perceived sweetness, low brass and woodwind tones raise bitterness, louder crunch makes crisps taste fresher, and noise above about 86 dB dulls salt and sweet.
crossover.title: Sonic seasoning

headline: Decaying fruit and insect albums

items.deep:
In the Decomposition works, clips pierce pieces of fruit on a table. Circuitry reads their changing moisture as they ripen and rot, and turns it into signals for light and sound, so lamps salvaged from local refuse flicker unpredictably. In Moré Moré (Leaky), pumped water runs through suspended tubing to hit cymbals and tick a triangle, and water leaks through stacked bathroom sinks.

Other parts use fans blowing on strands of wire, dripping firehoses and bells pulled by wires. Wood-cased speakers play long, reversed woodwind notes. The work grew out of a residency that began in May and marks 20 years of Curve commissions. For anyone building installations, it is a clear example of cheap sensors and found objects making sound that is never the same twice.
items.take: Yuko Mohri's site-responsive commission for the Barbican's Curve gallery opened on 1 October and runs until 24 January 2027, with free entry. Fruit wired to sensors, water-struck cymbals and salvaged lamps make a slowly shifting concert with no performer. ArtReview's critic calls it one of the strongest statements on contemporary Britain.
items.title: Yuko Mohri's 'In Concert' turns decay and leaks into sound at the Barbican Curve

items.deep:
João Machado's Meliponica processes recordings of Brazilian stingless bees into club tracks. Eternal Compost Community Band's Bug Noise makes harsh noise from wasps, dragonflies, butterflies and beetles. Bardo Todol and H. Flora built Honeybee Pollination Service from recordings they sent each other between Argentina and Germany: woodpeckers, cicadas, bats and domestic sounds.

Closer to Bolzano, Hannes Strobl's Resonance IBK records vehicles in the Innsbruck valley, where the mountains amplify them, and adds bass, horns and voice. Marja Ahti and John McCowen set clarinet against Reykjavik street recordings, Ilia Belorukov layers stairwells and underpasses with synths, and Synthetic Water Music blurs recorded water and synthesis across 51 tracks.
items.take: Matthew Blackwell's monthly column picks ten releases, an unusual number of them built on insect recordings. It also includes Hannes Strobl's piece on traffic sound in the Innsbruck valley and a 51-track water compilation.
items.title: Bees, wasps and valley traffic: Bandcamp's best field recordings of September

items.deep:
The 13th edition on 26 September drew more than 500 people. The Project Hail Mary panel, moderated by Dallas Taylor, focused on three problems: loneliness, space and creature vocals. DreamWorks' panel with Brian Chumney, Leff Lefferts and Gary A. Rizzo looked at myth and magic in the sound of Forgotten Island, moderated by Timothy Muirhead of Tonebenders.

The day opened with a keynote on fear, tension and the psychology of sound, with supervisor Karen Baker Landers and composer Tyler Bates. Other panels covered the Emmy-winning sound of Spider-Noir and Beef and the craft of horror soundtracks. The report is short on technique, but it maps which teams and which problems are shaping this awards season.
items.take: Mix's report from its Sound for Film & TV event at Sony Pictures Studios covers a Project Hail Mary panel with E2 Sound's Ethan Van der Ryn and Erik Aadahl and mixer Michael Semanick. Skywalker Sound's team also spoke on DreamWorks' Forgotten Island.
items.title: Project Hail Mary's sound team on loneliness, space and creature vocals

items.deep:
Applicants need an existing practice in collaborative spatial sound experimentation and must be available every day from 10:00 to 19:00. The lab mixes theory sessions with hands-on work. Selection is by Jan St. Werner, Michael Akstaller and members of SPR.

Participants get a CTM festival pass and invitation letters for visa or funding applications. Travel and accommodation are not covered, so a mobility grant such as Culture Moves Europe would be needed. The call asks for proposals in the applicant's own voice and says AI tools should only support brainstorming or translation.
items.take: CTM Festival is choosing up to six solo artists or researchers worldwide for a four-day spatial sound lab at silent green, Berlin, from 21 to 24 January 2027. Applications close on 15 October at 23:59 CET.
items.title: CTM 2027 Spatial Audio Experimentation Lab: deadline 15 October

items.take: At the 78th Prix Italia in L'Aquila, Sveriges Radio won radio documentary with a piece about a mother and daughter living with Alzheimer's. ORF won radio music with a Prince portrait built from music, sound design and a personal story, and Yle won radio drama with Maitotyttö (Milkmaid). The jury praised how fully the ORF piece used every sound as part of the narrative.
items.title: Prix Italia 2026 radio prizes go to Sweden, Austria and Finland

items.take: The 30th Phonurgia Nova awards gave the field recording jury prize unanimously to Dorota Blaszczak's 13-minute Multi-tone Soundscape (Poland), for its look at coexistence between human and non-human. The public prize went to Virginie Thurre's Le chant des glaciers valaisans (Switzerland). Anaïs Carton's La fragilité won the documentary jury prize, and the 2027 SACEM residencies will be announced on 14 November.
items.title: Phonurgia Nova 2026: Dorota Blaszczak wins the field recording prize

items.take: Dehli Musikk's Overtonium builds sound from 32 sine partials, each of which can be tuned, panned, muted and soloed. Retuning partials gives other temperaments and inharmonic spectra. It is free in VST3, AU and LV2 for macOS, Windows and Linux; Gearnews' round-up also lists the free Ultiverb reverb and ENS-86 chorus.
items.title: Overtonium: a free additive synth with 32 retunable partials

items.take: BLEASS's new reverb splits the signal into frequency components so decay, attack and stereo width can be drawn per range on spectral maps. It adds freeze, input filtering, sidechain and processors such as a spectral gate, ducker and pitch shifter. It costs €39 on desktop (including Linux, a first for BLEASS) and $12.99 on iOS.
items.title: BLEASS Spectral Reverb sets decay and width per frequency band

items.take: FRCTL Audio's GRNi Lite plays any dropped sample as grain clouds, one per held note, controlled by root, grain size and density. It is free with no serial or time limit, in VST3 and CLAP for Windows, macOS and Linux and AU on Mac. The paid GRNi adds a second layer, scales, modulation and effects.
items.title: GRNi Lite: a free three-knob granular sampler

items.take: Florida Atlantic University researchers played 100–800 Hz bands and a 10 kHz control through an underwater speaker, measured levels with calibrated hydrophones and filmed sharks by drone. Wild blacktip sharks reacted from up to 74 m, more than 70% of responses came in the acoustic far field, and they oriented away from the source. Sharks have no swim bladder and sense particle motion through the inner ear.
items.title: Blacktip sharks hear low sounds from 74 metres and turn away

items.take: The Innsbruck company launched the first fully implantable cochlear implant, with its microphone under about 6 mm of skin above and behind the ear. The battery lasts up to 40 hours and charges through an external GoPod. It has the CE mark and is available in Europe but not the US; 40 people had received it at launch.
items.title: MED-EL's TICI UNICO puts the whole cochlear implant under the skin

items.take: The Swiss festival offers three solo artists a residency from 17 May to 27 June 2027, with CHF 4,000 plus up to CHF 2,000 for travel, meals and materials. The theme is how stories, rumour and sound circulate. Sound art and instrument building are eligible, but sound installations with no visual dimension are excluded.
items.title: Schlossmediale Werdenberg 2027 residency on the theme KLATSCH: deadline 18 October

items.take: 3dSam's free firmware gives the cheap FM-1 three synth layers and a drum machine with 34 kits. There are nine engines including FM, phase distortion and granular, plus hand-recorded loops without a click, polymeter and a web editor. The code is on GitHub.
items.title: SLOOP: open-source firmware turns the M-VAVE FM-1 into a groovebox

items.take: The student nominees include audio pieces from Germany, Belgium, Denmark and the Czech Republic. Public online voting runs 12–15 October, and the awards are livestreamed from Berlin on 16 October.
items.title: PRIX EUROPA Rising Star: four student audio works nominated

items.take: Ikeda's installation, in which visitors lie under a large LED ceiling while sound and image are built from scientific datasets, returns to 180 Studios from 14 October to 20 December. It extends his data-verse project, ranging from particle physics to astrophysics.
items.title: Ryoji Ikeda's data-cosm [n°1] returns to London

items.take: The EU scheme pays artists living in Creative Europe countries, Italy included, €85 a day plus a travel allowance for 7–60 day stays abroad, with top-ups for green travel and access needs. Music is an eligible field. Later rounds close at the end of November, January, February, March and April.
items.title: Culture Moves Europe individual mobility grants: next deadline 31 October

items.take: Tidemark Theatre in Campbell River installed a hybrid assistive listening system. Auracast broadcasts straight to compatible hearing aids and earbuds without an app, while a Wi-Fi system streams to a free phone app.
items.title: A Canadian theatre streams its sound to hearing aids over Auracast

label: Mon 5 Oct 2026
lead: Yuko Mohri opened a free show at the Barbican Curve in which ripening fruit and leaking water drive sound and light. Bandcamp's September field recording column leaned heavily on insects, and Phonurgia Nova gave its field recording prize to Dorota Blaszczak. At Mix Sound for Film & TV, the Project Hail Mary team talked about creature vocals and the sound of isolation. CTM's spatial audio lab and a paid Swiss sound art residency both close in mid-October.

listen.why: Ferrari made a day-long recording of the environmental sound at a beach in Yugoslavia and edited it down to about 21 minutes, from daybreak onwards. It was composed between 1967 and 1970 and is regarded as a classic of composing with ambient recordings, which became a central part of his musical language.
listen.work: Presque rien No. 1 (Le lever du jour au bord de la mer)

radar.note: Caterina Barbieri's festival runs 10–24 October with 130 artists; Keiji Haino receives the Golden Lion and Sarah Davachi the Silver Lion.
radar.title: Biennale Musica 2026, A Child of Sound, Venice

radar.note: Festival 11–16 October; student public vote 12–15 October.

seed.note:
Schizophonia is the Canadian composer R. Murray Schafer's word for the split between an original sound and its electroacoustic reproduction. He introduced it in The New Soundscape, a handbook for music teachers published by BMI Canada in 1969, and returned to it in later writing on the soundscape.

Before recording, a sound existed only at the moment and place it was made. Recording and transmission let it be stored, copied and played anywhere. Schafer coined the term with a deliberately uneasy ring, to stress what he saw as the costs of that separation for listeners and for society.
